 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the claimant in O.P (MV) No.410 of 2009 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Irinjalakuda.
The respondents herein are the respondents before the tribunal.

2. According to the appellant/claimant, on 08.12.2008 at about 4:30 a.m., while the petitioner was travelling in a car bearing registration no. KL-45/4444, driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner, capsized when reached near Abco Steel at Udupi, as a result of which the petitioner sustained injuries.
The appellant approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 1 3,72,000/- limited to 6,00,000/-.
3. The 1st respondent, driver of the offending vehicle, filed a written statement admitting the accident but disputed the quantum of compensation claimed under each head.

The 2nd respondent insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy but disputing the quantum of compensation claimed as 2025:KER:58744 MACA NO. 978 OF 2015 well as the policy in respect of the vehicle.
Before the tribunal, PW 1 and RWs 1 and 2 were examined.
Exts.A1 to A11 and Ext.B1 were marked.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 2,39,630/-
as compensation under different heads with interest @7.5% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate costs from the 1st respondent-driver.
Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant has come up in appeal.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent insurance company.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant claims enhancement mainly under the following heads :-
Notional income :-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that though an amount of 6,000/- was claimed as the monthly income, the tribunal has taken only an amount of 3,500/-.

The learned counsel for the appellant further submitted that,
Even going by the judgment in 2025:KER:58744 MACA NO. 978 OF 2015 Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd.
[(2011) 13 SCC 236], the monthly income of a coolie ought to have been fixed at 6,500/- per month, since the accident occurred in the year 2008.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd.
[(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the fact that the injured was a driver by profession, in order to award a just compensation, I find it is appropriate to refix the monthly income as 7,000/-.
Loss of earnings :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that towards the head loss of earnings, the tribunal has taken only a period of three months for awarding compensation.

The appellant had sustained following injuries :-
"multiple abrasion on face, lacerated wound on the scalp and comminuted subtrochanteric fracture of femur (R) side".

2
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, I find that a period of six months can be taken for awarding compensation under the afore head.
Since the notional monthly income is refixed at 7,000/-, the total compensation payable under the head is recalculated thus: 42,000/- (7,000x6).
The tribunal has already awarded an amount of 10,500/- under the said head.

2025:KER:58744 MACA NO. 978 OF 2015 Thus, there will be an additional amount of 31,500/-
under the head loss of earnings.

Bystander expenses :- Though an amount of 25,000/- was claimed by the appellant towards bystander expenses, the tribunal had granted only an amount of 4,200/- at the rate of 150/- per day for a period of 28 days.

Considering the year of accident as well as the period of hospitalisation,
I am inclined to grant at the rate of 200/- per day for a period of 28 days.
Therefore, the total compensation would come to 5,600/- under the said head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 1,400/- under the afore head.
Pain and sufferings :-
The learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 20,000/- under the head, pain and sufferings, which is on the lower side.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained as well as the age of the claimant, I find that a total amount of 30,000/- can be awarded under the said head.
Therefore, there will be an additional amount of 10,000/- under the afore head.

2025:KER:58744 MACA NO. 978 OF 2015 Loss of amenities :- The learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 25,000/- under the said head which is on the lower side.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained as well as the age of the claimant, I find that a total amount of 30,000/- can be awarded towards loss of amenities.
Therefore, there will be an additional amount of 5,000/- under the afore head.
Permanent Disability/Loss of earning power :-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that as per Ext.A8 disability certificate, the percentage of disability was assessed as 14.30%.
However, the tribunal has reduced the percentage of disability to 14%.
The doctor who issued Ext.A8 deposed that the appellant has difficulty in continuing his occupation as a driver.
Considering the afore facts, I find that the functional disability can be fixed as 18%.

The learned counsel for the appellant fairly submitted that the appellant was aged 32 as per Ext.A10, driving license and not 28 at the time of accident and the appropriate multiplier to be adopted is 16, and not 17.

Going by the judgment in Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport 2025:KER:58744 MACA NO. 978 OF 2015 Corporation [2010(2)
KLT 802(SC)], the multiplier to be adopted is 16 and not 17 for the age group 30-35.

Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport 2025:KER:58744 MACA NO. 978 OF 2015 Corporation [2010(2)
KLT 802(SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the monthly income has been refixed as 7,000/-, the compensation for the head, permanent disability is recalculated as 2,41,920/- (7,000x12x16x18/100).
Since, the tribunal has already awarded an amount of 99,960/-, there will be an additional amount of 1,41,960/- under the afore head.

6. Though the appellant claimed enhancement of compensation under the other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the tribunal under other heads, since it appears to be just and reasonable.

3 7.
The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that the policy issued in respect of the offending car was a comprehensive one.

In paragraph 10 of the award, the tribunal found that the petitioner was not engaged as a driver at the time of accident which is required to cover the policy under proviso (II) to clause (a) of Section 147(1) of the MV Act and exonerated the insurer from the liability.
Since the policy issued was a comprehensive policy, all the afore facts are not relevant in this case.
The insurer is liable to pay the compensation awarded by the tribunal and the enhanced amount awarded by this court.
The direction of the tribunal to exonerate the insurance company from indemnifying the first respondent is to be set aside.

8. Thus, the impugned award of the tribunal is modified as follows:-

Bystander
5,600 expenses
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part.
The direction of the tribunal exonerating the insurance company from indemnifying the first respondent, insurer is set aside.

The appellants/claimants is awarded an additional compensation of 1,89,860/- (Rupees one lakh eighty nine thousand eight hundred and sixty only) over and above the compensation awarded by the tribunal with interest @7.5% per annum from the date of petition till realization and proportionate costs.

The 2nd respondent insurer shall deposit the said amount as well as the amount awarded by the tribunal together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The claimant shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, ADHAAR Card and bank details before the respondent insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the insurance company to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the 2025:KER:58744 MACA NO. 978 OF 2015 insurance company to deposit the said amount before the tribunal.
Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the appellant at the earliest in accordance with law.
